question_text: The bear grew up but 'he was a most amiable bear'. Give three examples to prove this.
answer_text: He was a most amiable bear as he did not harm anybody. He sat outside his kennel and looked with his small intelligent eyes most amicably at the cattle grazing in the field near by. The children rode on his back and had more than once been found asleep in his kennel, between his two paws. The three dogs loved to play various kinds of games with him. They pulled his ears and his stump of a tail, teasing him in every way. However, he did not mind it in the least.
final_answer: The bear was amiable as he did not harm anyone, played with children, and tolerated teasing from dogs.

question_text: What happened one Sunday when the lady was going to her sister's house? What did the lady do? What was the bear's reaction?
answer_text: One Sunday when the lady was going to her sister's house, she saw a bear coming along at full speed. Thinking that he was her pet, the lady got very angry. Being already late for lunch, she scolded him and told him to go back. She saw that he had even lost his new collar. This made her angrier, and she hit him on his nose with her parasol. The parasol broke in two. The bear opened his mouth several times as if he wanted to say something, and then it turned around and went on its way.
final_answer: The lady mistakenly scolded the bear, thinking it was her pet, and the bear reacted by turning away sadly.
difficulty_reasoning: Involves understanding the context and emotions of both characters.

question_text: Why was the bear looking sorry for himself in the evening? Why did the cook get angry with her mistress?
answer_text: The bear was looking sorry for himself in the evening because he had been chained all day and he could not do his usual activities. When his mistress returned, she scolded him, thinking that it was him she saw in the forest. She said that as punishment, he would have to remain chained for two more days. The cook loved the bear as her child and could not bear to see the bear being scolded like that. This was why she got angry. She told the mistress that the bear had been very good the whole day, and had been sitting outside his kennel, looking at the gate and waiting for her to come back.
final_answer: The bear felt sorry for being chained, and the cook got angry because she felt the bear was unfairly punished.
